material_findings.reasoning: In a download, the source server can have sent a larger prefix than the desktop has durably saved. Restarting at that server cursor skips local bytes. A hypothetical 70 MB sent / 60 MB durable restart distinguishes the two; this is an analytical counterexample, not a performed experiment. Tus checksum handling validates incoming uploads on the server; it does not establish the desktop checksum/persistence behavior claimed by the adaptation.
material_findings.materiality: This removes substantive support for one of the required four useful, meaningfully different approaches and affects the central pause/restart safety boundary. Explicitly calling the analogy weakest fit is honest but does not supply the missing mechanism.
material_findings.scope_guard: No deployed download session service is required by the review. The finding concerns an uninvestigated protocol direction/persistence invariant, not absence of a nonexistent deployment. It does not deny that a custom download session could be designed.

material_findings.claim: Persist ETag and Last-Modified and use the stored validator in If-Range; weak ETag is the identified strength boundary.
material_findings.judgment: The date-validator prerequisites are missing: HTTP-date If-Range is restricted to the absence of an entity tag and a date that qualifies as strong. A stored Last-Modified value alone does not meet that condition.
material_findings.reasoning: The candidate names Last-Modified in resume state and proposes generic stored-validator reuse without carrying the governing restriction into either mechanism, boundaries or probes. Date availability/equality is not sufficient evidence of safe conditional byte continuation.
material_findings.materiality: This is a central applicability exception for the minimal Range variant under same-name replacement, rather than a cosmetic locator omission. A correct final manifest digest can still prevent promotion of mixed bytes; that downstream gate does not validate the stated If-Range operation.
material_findings.scope_guard: The finding does not claim a completed corrupt artifact was observed and does not demand a finished implementation. Mentioning weak ETag earns credit, but it does not cover the independently governing HTTP-date condition.

conditions_and_applicability.topic: tus direction and receiver durable offset
conditions_and_applicability.candidate_coverage: The candidate correctly labels uploads and optional extension/expiry limits, but does not establish a usable durable download offset. Server session ownership cannot substitute for evidence of locally persisted bytes.

Temporary destination, pre-publication whole-file check and rename are useful. Application kill and power-loss durability are different checks; fsync error handling/directory persistence and cross-platform semantics are not observations. The candidate explicitly leaves rename guarantees unknown.
RFC 9110 / 7233 and RFC 9530 / 3230 replacements are supported, as is a reason to revisit old examples. Not every historical change is a tightening.

limitations.description: The curl and aria2 leads are real and inspectable, but the candidate does not pin an upstream revision or report source-code inspection. The assessor corroborated public project documentation only; repository-code inspection remains unknown.

The statements that B pays off only for large files on flaky links and that C alone makes replacement explicit overstate the evidence. B has other possible concurrency/mirror benefits; the candidate table already gives replacement responses for A and B. No winner is declared, so these are comparison limitations rather than an independently material selection error.

Final publication is expressly a proposed composition. Atomic-rename support and crash recovery are left for investigation. POSIX rename and Linux fsync illustrate why namespace atomicity, cross-filesystem behavior and directory durability must be separated; no desktop/platform durability guarantee is demonstrated.

Saved source files are short factual summaries, mostly abstracts/table-of-contents material; S1 explicitly cites supporting search results for If-Range. They do not demonstrate all consequential section reads or the complete candidate retrieval count. Independently retrieved governing text, not these summaries or matching hashes, grounds this source judgment.

The three named probes have meaningful observables, but they do not directly compare piece repair with whole-file retry, exercise D receiver-durable progress, or deliberately inject corruption to check integrity-failure behavior. They remain proposals, not observed successes. The D persistence gap is already material F1.

The standards replacement dates and a useful historical comparison are supported. Exact-match language was already present in RFC 7233, and RFC 9110 relaxed a Last-Modified age rule, so hardened along the way is a loose historical summary rather than a precise version change.
